questions.question: Should we pull other mods' gems and minerals into our own mods, or control them where they sit?

options.label: Control them, absorb small pieces only (Recommended)
options.description: Why recommended: one registry already decides where every mod's mineral appears, so owning the files buys no extra control. Buys: no licence trouble, donor fixes keep arriving, little porting. Costs: we can't restyle a donor gem without porting it, and we still depend on those mods. Small ports (e.g. the fossil seams) happen only where they remove real upkeep.

options.label: Absorb the gem and crystal mods
options.description: Buys: Jewelry's gems and the Minerals crystals become ours to rename, re-art and rebalance. Costs: weeks of porting a large code framework, Jewelry is non-commercial share-alike, Glowstone has no licence at all, and we lose their updates.

options.label: Absorb every mineral mod
options.description: Buys: total ownership, no outside dependency for any material. Costs: largest effort by far, two mods cannot legally be copied, and the registry has to be built anyway, so the control gain is nearly nothing.

questions.question: What unit should the settings screen use for how much of a mineral a biome holds?

options.label: Amount per map (Recommended)
options.description: Why recommended: it answers the question a player actually asks. Example: 'gold 1,500 per map, about 1 deposit'. Buys: easy to reason about, and it converts straight into deposits. Costs: a rock-poor flat map can come in under the number, so the screen shows an estimate.

options.label: Deposits per map
options.description: Buys: matches what you see on the map. Costs: a deposit of gold and a deposit of steel are very different amounts, so comparing materials gets harder.

options.label: Ore per 1,000 rock cells
options.description: Buys: a true 'ore grade', honest on any terrain. Costs: does not fit nodules, crystals, sea floors or salvage, and is hard to picture.

questions.question: When a newly installed mod adds an ore the registry has never heard of, what should happen to it?

options.label: Keep it off the map until it gets a row (Recommended)
options.description: Why recommended: matches your 'carefully selected, period'. Buys: nothing appears anywhere by accident; a warning names it. Costs: a new mod's ore silently does nothing until someone adds its row.

options.label: Let it behave as the mod intended
options.description: Buys: new mods work out of the box. Costs: the random-outcrop problem comes back with every mineral mod added.

options.label: Refuse to start the game
options.description: Buys: impossible to miss. Costs: one unregistered ore blocks play until fixed.

questions.question: What should a quarry give in a biome that holds no quarryable minerals at all?

options.label: Only chunks of the local rock (Recommended)
options.description: Why recommended: follows your ruling, local materials only. Buys: no ore from nowhere. Costs: a quarry in those biomes is a stone source only.

options.label: A small trickle of steel
options.description: Buys: quarries stay useful everywhere. Costs: brings iron into biomes you ruled have none.

options.label: Quarry cannot be built there
options.description: Buys: the player is told up front. Costs: also blocks the quarry's stone and block output, which is local and fine.
